mu_name_from: MuMain maps MODEL_HELM + i to HelmMale{i+1}, so file 10 is armour index 9, which openmu names Plate.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateBoots(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, walkSpeed, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). Slot 6, so `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)` makes the group 11.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.walk_speed_note: Four, the boots' own column, which nothing in this simulation reads: a walk is MU's fixed tile rate. Recorded rather than dropped.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 1, 0 - the Dark Knight alone.
stats.shelf_note: On Martin's and Harold's shelf at +3 - the last column of the wandering merchants' stock, see shared/Market.cs - and until this row existed the shelf dropped the line, because a model with no row is a thing the realm cannot price. The five Plate pieces were built for the guards' bodies first and the row came second.

sheet_from: MuMain/src/bin/Data/Player - the tree that was not upscaled in place. remaster_one's Player/ holds 2x neural output written over MU's originals; see pipeline/find_source.py.
sheet_note: One sheet, which is why this part builds and the chest does not. The Plate gloves and boots are the only pieces of the set MU drew without a second texture on them.
